findings.title: Use raw login eligibility when deciding whether to invalidate
findings.body: `original` comes from `getById`, which wraps organization-linked providers so `isEnabled()` is false when their organization is disabled. If a cached provider belongs to a disabled organization and an update changes `linkOnly` or `hideOnLogin` to exclude it, both predicates here can be false, so this early return leaves the login-IDP cache intact. After the organization is enabled, the stale cached ID is returned and the login bean rechecks only `isEnabled()`, allowing the link-only or hidden provider to appear. Base invalidation on the persisted IDP login fields or otherwise invalidate when those fields change.

findings.title: Distinguish a missing organization ID from an empty one
findings.body: This maps both `organizationId == null` and `organizationId.equals("")` to the same search key. The provider contract treats null as no organization filter for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL`, but treats any non-null ID—including an empty string—as a specific organization filter. If the broad query is cached first, a call with an empty ID can incorrectly receive providers associated with other organizations; the reverse order can incorrectly hide them from the broad query.

findings.title: Cleanup uses an alias that was never created
findings.body: The test creates providers with aliases such as `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`, but registers cleanup for the literal alias `alias` on every iteration. Those cleanup actions therefore do not remove the created providers (the later provider at alias `idp-alias-20` uses the same incorrect cleanup). If the test realm is reused, these records remain and can pollute subsequent tests.
